subject: glessner_frances_m_1904

shot.build: stage, tree c30a40136 + 4 uncommitted figure file(s)

silhouette.what: Silhouette and fit of the clothes
silhouette.note: Since the tailoring fix (human-gown.js, T-3553 round 3) the skirt is close over the hips and flares from about the knee to a hem about 1.5 times the hips' half-width (64 cm across, was 83), a little fuller behind: at 3 m it reads as the Met's gored skirt and the Easter skirts, no longer a crinoline. On the walk the skirt driver still opens the hem forward over the leading foot and back over the trailing one, so at mid-stride from the side the hem is a wider triangle than a standing woman's; the Easter women's hems break forward too, less. Jacket to the hip with a short peplum reads as the Met coat cut shorter.

folds.note: Seven gore seams are drawn as shallow valleys (about 2 mm against the gores) and below the knee the flare falls into soft folds (fourteen at the near level, seven at the next), with two rows of black braid at the hem. In black wool under the stage light the seams show only close up and as faint vertical shading at 3 m; the folds show as a fluted hem edge. They are fixed folds that ride with the skirt, not folds that break as the walk changes; the far levels (past 20 m) carry the cut but no folds.

hat_hair.note: A broad dark hat trimmed high with grey plumes over drawn-up hair: the Easter crowd and Mrs. Fairbanks wear the same kind, hers paler and heaped higher.

skin.note: Monochrome prints. Face and hands read at 3 m; the hands are warmer (orange) in the stage light than the face.

hands.note: Clasped in front at the waist; the crossed fingers are bulky at 3 m. The pictures show gloved or bare hands at the sides or raised.

stance.what: How the figure stands or sits
stance.note: Upright, feet hidden under the skirt, as the matrons stand.

motion.note: Mid-stride the skirt swings as one piece and the legs never show (test_human_skirt and test_human_gown hold it on the cut skirt); the hem opens forward over the leading foot more than the Easter women's do. The strip is shot on the stage, following her.

differences.picture: Gored skirt close at waist and hips, flaring from about the knee (Met 1902 suit); Easter 1904 skirts nearly columnar to the ground.
differences.ours: Close over the hips, flaring from about the knee to a hem about 1.5 times the hips' half-width (64 cm across, was 83), a little fuller behind; on the walk the hem opens forward and back with the legs.

differences.picture: Gore seams and braid at the hem (Met); folds at the hem when walking (Easter).
differences.ours: Seven shallow gore seams, soft fixed folds below the knee (near levels) and two rows of black braid at the hem; the seams are faint in black at 3 m, and the folds do not change with the stride.

differences.picture: Tall cream lace standing collar and a lace jabot falling from it (Fairbanks; Met bodice yoke).
differences.ours: Cream lace (net and flowers drawn on the cloth) over the standing collar, the pleated jabot and the top of the front; the cloth below brought up to cream. The collar is the asset's height, a little lower than Mrs. Fairbanks's, and the jabot is pleated cloth with the lace drawn on it, not a falling frill.

differences.picture: Lace frills at the wrists (Fairbanks); braided cuffs on the Met coat.
differences.ours: A cream lace frill flaring from inside each sleeve's end over the wrist (near levels, within 20 m), and soutache braid round the coat's cuffs.

differences.picture: Met coat to the upper thigh, lapels, buttoned below the bust, braid at cuffs and hem; Fairbanks coat open over a pale front.
differences.ours: Black jacket to the hip with a peplum, closed, no braid; pale front shows only as a narrow V.

differences.picture: Black wool suit (Met, in colour); dark coats in the monochrome prints.
Broad hat heaped with pale plumes (Fairbanks), broad hats trimmed high (Easter).
differences.ours: Broad black hat, grey plumes; less heaped, darker plumes.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever laid the stills beside the pictures; each checklist item is {what, status, note} with status open | reads | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling — open when a visitor would see the figure is not the pictures’ kind of person in that respect. The first figure of each role is the owner’s call (the plan’s "Your call"); later figures of the role are held to the one he approved. A reshoot of a changed figure (bound) sets the verdict back to unreviewed.
